steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Reed, how's it goin' over there?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Yes, no problem.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Huff—Alright! That's the last tent we've got to put up.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Wow, you two are a powerful pair.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Right, you were taking off, weren't you?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Aye, Chenchen and I are investigatin' those 'spectres' that were under Arts control. We've still got other assignments once everythin's done here.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: This is the edge of County Trent. No barracks'll be comin' lookin' for trouble no more.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: *sigh*... If only we'd been better at maintaining order. Wouldn't have had all this commotion and unjust treatment.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Huh? What are you on about? If it weren't for all of you, there's no chance we would've made it this far.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: If this were me own home, I'd be treating all of you to a nip of elderflower liqueur tonight. I'd even be giving the stuff away.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: But most of the supplies we have on hand come from that... 'Rhodes Island' you lot're from, haha.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: If we write to Rhodes Island, will you get the message? We'll be letting you know once we're settled somewhere. If you're ever back in the area, drop by and say hi.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh, maybe? Once Victoria's war comes to an end, plus there's someone Chenchen should be meeting...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: What about you, Reed? Where are you goin' next?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I... I think I'll make sure everyone has settled down, before I take care of my own business.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Even though they are away from the Scáthanna Fields, their crimes, and the hand of the lights-out bell... the Tarans still live in muddied lands, trapped where they stand.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I think... I need to help them come up with ideas.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I can speak both Taran and Victorian. If we enter the cities later on, we'll run into people of all kinds, and I can help negotiate... At least, I could do it more easily than others.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, right, when you went lookin' for the Rhodes Island safehouse today, did you get followed by anyone?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I don't think so...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's okay. Thank you for reminding me. If those soldiers are here for me... I won't be afraid.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: And also... thank you for your kindness.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Say, will you sell me a tent when the time comes?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: The factories in the cities make that canvas. They don't leak water even when they get rained on for half a month. Just perfect for me to retrofit my trolley with.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: She's a fair kind-hearted one, and I'm sure you'll be fair when it comes to naming the price. I think you two'd have no trouble reaching a deal.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Haha, I'm joking. Where would I find the money for something this nice?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Who would've thought, though? We were just trying to figure out how to survive a couple days ago, but now we get to sleep in these sturdy old factory-made tents. We can even light fires at night.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Aye. They're a capable bunch.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: And they know Oripathy well.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: (Whistles)

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: (Incoherently rhythmic whistles)

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: O, mists that shroud the valley... ♪

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: ...Hide her figure waying far... ♪

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: It's a beautiful song, that.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Out of all the people who've fancied me... you might be the only one who still remembers me.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Don't be saying that now... I'm certain everyone remembers.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: This Oripathy's not your fault.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: (Whistles slightly off-key)

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh*.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: That lad, Selmon's brother, he's gone. That whole Dublinn squad we helped out, they might just be gone, too.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We did all that for nothing.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: At least... you're still alive. You went missing for so long, but you're still alive.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I saw Reed handing you some medicine. Is Oripathy really curable, then?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: No, they said there's no cure for it.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: But please don't be blaming those Dublinn soldiers. I hid them in the factory's lorries, and raw Originium ore shards got in their wounds... This isn't their fault.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I'm not blaming. I'm just feeling awful.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: The rest of you had faith in Dublinn, but I didn't have what it takes. Dublinn's more impressive than any of us. They've got weapons, too. But we all saw what happened to that squad in the end.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Dublinn treats us well and lets our Taran voices be heard, but after that? It beats me... All I remember is the blood I saw on the lorries that day.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Even now, Selmon still wants to find Dublinn to fight the Victorians, and I can't pull her out of it.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: She and Reed were chatting for so long that day, say. Did Reed not talk even a little sense into her?

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I don't think it's bad that Selmon wants to do this. A colleen like her's got much to accomplish for other Tarans.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Do you remember? Not long after I got infected myself, the entire Infected district was chased out of town.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: It was the stronger of us, after that, that took everything they could lay their hands on from the rest of us exiles. Left behind only frail pensioners and children, and the ones like me ailing badly from the sickness.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You should've told us sooner rather than keep it all to yourself. At the very least, it would've spared you some pain.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: To tell the truth, I can hardly remember any of it. I can't remember why no one fought back, why no one tried to protect one another.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: I always used to think that was just how life was. Doesn't matter what's in your hands when you're starving, you close your eyes and tuck in.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Lisa died at the bottom of the mine. So did Clodagh. Has your family ever complained about working the mines?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er... I couldn't say, really—maybe it's how hard it is to blame someone for it. But at the very least, I did feel... right terrible when my sisters died.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I wanted to find someone to talk to about it, but it was dark and suffocating at the bottom of those mines, and no one had the time to listen. I got out to peddle my wares around, and it turned out everyone had their own troubles already. No one had an ear to lend to me.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: But hey, not too late to talk now.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: Right you are. It's not too late now.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: The wood we've gathered should be enough to last us through the night.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: (Whistles) ...Let's go, then. Won't be so easy for you to tell the way once the sun comes down.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hey, the pot's bubbling. Can I have a bite now?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Settle down there, you cottonhead! Did you not ever cook supper back home?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Wait inside the tent. Once the meat's done, give me a hand bringing it over.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: She seems to be in a better mood.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Yes... but I'm sure she's still grieving.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: It's a good thing you killed her heart for Dublinn, at the very least.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...You knew?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: And I imagine with you here, they won't stray onto the wrong path.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Though it'll be hard for you to keep walking with them, Draco.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I'm not wrong when it comes to these things.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Don't be daft, Fergal, you played King Gaeil's warrior in last year's play. Three times you fell with 'mortal wounds', three times you had to clamber back up. Your arms and legs were all bruised by the end.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Then I'll make him invincible this year. Every year, King Gaeil loses in battle, Gastrell dies at the bottom of the castle. Other than the costumes, we never try anything new.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hey, Selmon, c'mere. Have a seat. I've been thinking you could take on the role of King Gaeil's left-hand man, the general, this year. Yeah, you're a bit young, but there's not one of us with more fire in their belly than you.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: What?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: You're only saying that 'cause you saw the pot she's bringing over. Look, she doesn't want to.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: No, what are you talking about? I don't know who that is.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Eh? Don't they put on those plays every summer over by yours? We're trying to sort out who'll be playing which role.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Mmm... is that where someone calls herself the goddess of the river and splashes the audience at the end? That whole thing?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I've seen it... but I'm not interested. Not unless I'm playing her.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: That's her mourning the dead soldiers. Her lines are harder to remember than any other role.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Oh.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: We might not finish building the theater before the end of the summer, though. You could have till next year to prepare.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Right... who knows.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Looks like you still want to go after Dublinn?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Of course. You think I'm just going to give up like the rest of you?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I made my decision after talking to Reed that day.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: I still believe it. Dublinn's dream can be realized, and someone has to realize it.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...What is it you want to find out from me?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I have nothing to ask. I've seen what you've done for myself.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I trust the judgments I make seeing what I do, and I trust Rhodes Island's judgment.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But right now, in the eyes of most Victorians, there is only one Draco still alive.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Dublinn's Red Dragon, the descendant of the Taran king. More than enough to fill the dukes with their sinister ambitions and the nobles with anxiety.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: It must be difficult for you.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Does... she know my identity, then?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Bagpipe?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: She is actually very smart, and attentive, but there's a great deal she doesn't like to think negatively about—especially not friends she approves of.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: If we continue our journey together, that's something that both you and her will have to face eventually.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Are you... advising me to leave as soon as I can?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: What's done can't be undone. You can't run from the responsibilities you have to bear.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But I think that, to some people, whether you are a Draco or not doesn't actually matter so much.

steps.name: Hoarse Singing
steps.text: By tender stream that brushes on and through the upland grass ♪

steps.name: Hoarse Singing
steps.text: We make a toast to those of us not here to raise their glass ♪

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Someone's singing.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...It's probably Fergal.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Is this Taran?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Yes. It sounds like... it's about wine, and the uplands in summer. I've never heard it before... but it's beautiful.
Bid flap your wings to wake by light, wee fowl upon the bays ♪
Bear off the news we gather round, along and with the waves ♪

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They're... all so happy.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I can tell.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But all they have are their tents and fire.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Then I'm sure they'll be even happier when they have their houses and farmland.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Let's head inside.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Chenchen, you're finally back! Here, look at this! Mr. Odhrán can whistle with a blade of grass!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: (Whistles sharply)

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Haha, my pitch can be pretty off. My da was really good at it, though. I picked up a bit here and there from him.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Hmm—hm-hmm—

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, you don't mind if I sing along a little, do you?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Go ahead! It's our drinking song. Only thing I'll take offense to is an empty bottle, haha.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: What's the lyrics, then? Is it okay if I sing in Victorian?

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Hm... Let me fetch someone else. You just listen to them.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Fionn, you're up.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh*...
'Ever does this land well with tears, yet we drink only of bygone dews and flames.'

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: By winding lane that blooms with rose and bellflow'r on the loam ♪

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: You're out of tune! That's terrible!

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Shut up! Not like you're any better!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: (Sharp whistle)

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Ugh... I'm begging you, enough of that noise. You've got some bloody novel way of arguing...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Oi, no throwing stones either! What if we actually got hit here?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Wow, that bread smells good...

steps.name: Young Refugee
steps.text: You can have half!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Oh, ta! Here, Chenchen, you have a bite. Come on, just one.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Lush, isn't it? I wonder what herbs they're usin'...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Hmm... Can't tell.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Eh? You spent ages back in Yan. What, did your taste buds get more fussy, or just duller a bit?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: What do you think? We Lungmenites brew our tea in the summer with twenty-four kinds of medicinal herbs.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Really...? Oh, you're pullin' my leg again, aren't you?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I'm not.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: ...Are you enjoying yourself, Reed?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: This is how their lives could've been all along. A bit better than this too, of course.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: You gave them their lives back.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Reed, you know Taran. No excuses from you. Sing!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: (Teasing whistle) Sing.

a.text: Fare on and long, you traveler, but to where do you now roam? ♪

steps.name: Special Forces Soldier
steps.text: The transport will leave clear tracks in the mud. Should we take a detour?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: No need. We'll head straight to our destination.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Good stuff. And you, Moran.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Miss Moran, what're you doin' sittin' so far off? Reed's told you a million times it's okay!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: She's right. Come on, 'Wandering Bard of the Glen of Camai...' Sing.

steps.name: Moran
steps.text: O, mists that shroud the valley... hide her figure waying far... ♪

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Well, gosh, I think I once heard this beautiful singing years ago.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I'm sure you have.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Right you are. I remember taking my sister around—she wasn't so sick that she couldn't walk yet. We were stood on the stone bridge, listening for a good while.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: *sigh* There must be more bridges like that, right? With just how far the Camai flows.

a.text: Bid breezes past the rugged lime ♪

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Bring the civilians under control first, but don't let any of them get hurt.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Our target possesses excellent military accomplishments. Avoid direct confrontation to all possible extents.

a.text: Pick me a flower for her ♪

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Selmon, look. How's this for defensive posture? Learned it from you.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: So? You'll just be chasing fowlbeasts from now on. What'd you learn that for?

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Do not talk to any of them. Not even a single word.

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Leave the rest to me.

a.text: Bare bottles chill the bones with hurt ♪

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Don't forget, we need to be out of here before daybreak.

a.text: We make a toast to those of us not here to raise their glass ♪

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Crossbows at the ready. Prepare smoke grenades.

a.text: The tears we cup to drink are all the same and one, my lass ♪

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh*... I'm hopping out for some fresh air.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Hm? Mist at this hour...?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You—

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Wh—

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: When did you...

steps.name: Fischer
steps.text: Good evening, sir.
